about.title: Modesto Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in Modesto never really stops. Emergency rooms and urgent care clinics across the city see a steady flow of patients, including many of the 1,992 people injured in local traffic collisions in 2025. Most of that care goes well. When it doesn't, a missed diagnosis, a medication error, or a surgical mistake can leave a Stanislaus County family facing a second injury on top of the first. California handles these claims under rules known as MICRA. The deadlines are short: generally one year from the date you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from when it happened. Before suit is filed, the provider must receive 90 days' notice. A qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records and confirm the care fell below the accepted standard, because a poor result by itself is not malpractice. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Modesto patients with an independent attorney who takes medical negligence cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated in Modesto after a crash and my injury got worse. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not automatically. Many of the 1,365 injury collisions reported in Modesto in 2025 sent people to local emergency rooms, and some conditions worsen even with proper care. Malpractice means a provider fell below the accepted standard and that failure caused harm. A qualified medical expert has to confirm that before a claim moves forward.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are treated separately. An attorney can explain how the current figures apply to your situation.
